newsitem.title: USA: Glickman tells Wisconsin he watching NE dairy deal.
newsitem.headline: Glickman tells Wisconsin he watching NE dairy deal.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said he was carefully watching a new six-state dairy agreement in New England and would cancel the deal if it produced any "negative" effects.
Glickman, speaking to reporters after addressing agricultural officials, said the Northeast Interstate Dairy Compact he approved August 9 must serve the public interest.

"If I find negative things happening, I will revoke the compact," Glickman said. "If it was used to raise milk prices to consumers, particularly poor consumers, or prejudice the free flow of milk between regions, I will revoke the compact."

The Compact, an item of dispute for six years that finally made it into the 1996 federal farm policy law, empowers a six-state commission to raise the price of fluid milk bound for retail stores by up to 25 percent.
The states involved are Massachusetts, Maine, Connecticut, New Hampshire, Vermont and Rhode Island.

Proponents said it would help northeast dairy farmers stay in business and assure adequate local milk supplies. But opponents including consumer groups said it will raise milk prices, inspire other regional "milk plans" to protect farm incomes, and prevent the free market from setting prices.
Wisconsin governor Tommy Thompson appealed to Glickman on Monday to repeal last month's approval of the deal.

"Secretary Glickman's decision to authorize the Northeast Interstate Dairy Compact is a direct attack on Wisconsin dairy farmers," Thompson said in a statement widely circulated by his office in this leading dairy producing state.
"Dairy policy is more complicated than nuclear physics," Glickman said. "The compact will have no impact specifically on Wisconsin. It's just not that big of a factor in the marketplace."
Glickman added that the legislatures and governors of each of the six Northeast states had approved the deal and consumer surveys had shown 92 to 95 percent approval of it.
"I didn't have much choice but to approve it," he said.
